rationale: Both require IAM requirements to be defined, documented, and approved.
A.5.15 covers both setting and implementing access rules. This control covers the setting part.
A.5.1 is the general rule for all security policies, of which the access control policy is one.
Both require the IAM requirements to be implemented.
Covers the implementation half of A.5.15.
Restricting access to information in line with the policy is part of implementing it.
Both require the full life cycle of identities to be managed.
NCA has no identity lifecycle control. It only requires periodic review of identities.
Username and password authentication is the stated minimum of this control.
Management of authentication secrets is included in this control.
A.8.5 covers secure authentication in general. The stronger methods are in UCF-IAM-05.
Both require MFA for remote access and privileged accounts based on an impact assessment.
A.8.5 requires authentication strength to match the access restrictions. MFA is one way to meet it.
MFA requirement specific to remote and webmail access to email.
Authentication factors for users of external web applications.
Same four principles: need-to-know, need-to-use, least privilege, segregation of duties.
A.8.3 restricts access per the policy. These principles are how the restriction is decided.
A.5.3 covers segregation of duties in general, not only in access rights.
The principles are normally stated in the access control policy.
Both require privileged access to be managed.
Both require privileged access rights to be restricted and managed.
Privileged utility programs are a specific case of privileged access.
Both cover granting, reviewing, changing, and removing access rights.
Periodic review of identities and access rights is one part of this control.
Review and immediate revocation of personnel powers at end of employment is one part of this control.
Return of assets at end of employment happens alongside access revocation.
Both require periodic review of how the IAM requirements are implemented.
A.5.36 requires compliance reviews for all policies, not only access control.
A.5.1 requires all policies to be reviewed at planned intervals.
Both require access to source code and development tools to be managed.
